queue_items.claim: The row's own close seam is supported by nothing but a tier-3 parashah mark; no tier-1 signal is named for it anywhere in the boundary field.
queue_items.grounds: boundary_rationale closes with only: 'It closes at web:Isa.42.25. A parashah PE mark (single-witness) closes at oshb:Isa.42.25, corroborating the break.' The mark is said to corroborate a break that no tier-1 signal in the row establishes, and prophets-parashah is never a boundary driver. Inventory check: MT 42:25 is PE (type correct). The signal that actually carries this seam is the divine-speech frame opening the next unit, וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte) -- one of only 4 koh-amar verses in chs 41-43 (MT 42:5, 43:1, 43:14, 43:16; 48 book-wide) -- which appears in this row only inside a device_notes name-pair thread and is never named as the close warrant. The seam location is sound; the warrant as shipped is not.
queue_items.proposed_change: Name the koh-amar onset at oshb:Isa.43.1 in the boundary field as the tier-1 signal carrying the close, with its pointed splice and tier, and keep the PE mark at oshb:Isa.42.25 as corroboration.

queue_items.claim: The fire-verb device straddling the row's own close seam is declared tier NONE; re-collation returns skeleton tier in one direction.
queue_items.grounds: device_notes: וַתִּבְעַר (oshb:Isa.42.25, tier: byte) 'is answered by' the clause at oshb:Isa.43.2, 'the two sharing only the fire-verb stem, the attested tokens returning tier NONE'. Re-collated: the attested token תִבְעַר (oshb:Isa.43.2, tier: byte) returns SKELETON tier against oshb:Isa.42.25; only the reverse direction returns none. Under the cross-seam cohesion rule a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity unless honestly disclosed, and understating the tier from skeleton to none understates that counter-pressure. The seam still holds on the koh-amar onset at oshb:Isa.43.1.
queue_items.proposed_change: Restate the pair at skeleton tier with the direction named.

queue_items.claim: The sole refusal ground for the row's strongest rival is an original-language form claim carried unspliced on the translation witness, and the unit's extent is described by a tier-4 chapter division.
queue_items.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative refuses an internal split because 'no fresh imperative, addressee, or divine-speech-frame formula opens web:Isa.42.21', then bounds the unit as running 'through to the chapter's close'. The form claim is boundary-relevant original-language content but ships with no pointed splice and keyed to the WEB witness; the extent clause rests on a chapter division, which is tier-4 metadata and never boundary evidence. Checked against the bytes, the form claim is true: MT 42:21 reads יְהוָ֥ה חָפֵ֖ץ לְמַ֣עַן צִדְק֑וֹ יַגְדִּ֥יל תּוֹרָ֖ה וְיַאְדִּֽיר (oshb:Isa.42.21, tier: byte) -- no speech frame, no imperative -- so the rival is rightly refused, on a ground the row does not evidence to standard.
queue_items.proposed_change: Splice MT 42:21 and cite it as oshb:Isa.42.21 for the absence-of-frame ground, and replace 'through to the chapter's close' with the verse-anchored extent (through web:Isa.42.25).

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The opening verse of this unit is web:Isa.42.18, “Hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see.”, pointed הַחֵרְשִׁ֖ים שְׁמָ֑עוּ וְהַעִוְרִ֖ים הַבִּ֥יטוּ לִרְאֽוֹת (oshb:Isa.42.18, tier: byte), a fresh imperative address to the deaf and blind, distinct from the third-person idol-trusters closing the previous span. A parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness) sits at oshb:Isa.42.17, immediately before this unit's own onset. The addressee is named at web:Isa.42.19, “Who is blind, but my servant? Or who is as deaf as my messenger whom I send? Who is as blind as he who is at peace, and as blind as Yahweh’s servant?”, pointed מִ֤י עִוֵּר֙ כִּ֣י אִם עַבְדִּ֔י וְחֵרֵ֖שׁ כְּמַלְאָכִ֣י אֶשְׁלָ֑ח מִ֤י עִוֵּר֙ כִּמְשֻׁלָּ֔ם וְעִוֵּ֖ר כְּעֶ֥בֶד יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.42.19, tier: byte), identified by the common noun servant without further identifying the referent. It closes at web:Isa.42.25. A parashah PE mark (single-witness) closes at oshb:Isa.42.25, corroborating the break.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this unit at web:Isa.42.21-Isa.42.22, where the description shifts from the deaf-and-blind servant's own failure to the plundered people's suffering, was considered and set aside because no fresh imperative, addressee, or divine-speech-frame formula opens web:Isa.42.21; the plundered-people description continues answering the same rebuke opened at web:Isa.42.18-Isa.42.19 through to the chapter's close.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: rebuke of a blind and deaf servant figure, closing in an account of plunder and unheeded judgment
shipped_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
shipped_row.device_notes: The closing verse reads in full, web:Isa.42.25, “Therefore he poured the fierceness of his anger on him, and the strength of battle. It set him on fire all around, but he didn’t know. It burned him, but he didn’t take it to heart.”, pointed וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֤ךְ עָלָיו֙ חֵמָ֣ה אַפּ֔וֹ וֶעֱז֖וּז מִלְחָמָ֑ה וַתְּלַהֲטֵ֤הוּ מִסָּבִיב֙ וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֔ע וַתִּבְעַר בּ֖וֹ וְלֹא יָשִׂ֥ים עַל לֵֽב (oshb:Isa.42.25, tier: byte). The servant addressed here is named by the common noun 'my servant' and by 'Yahweh's servant' at web:Isa.42.19, a spare designation this row does not expand; whether this figure is the same one presented at web:Isa.42.1 or a distinct referent is a held question this row does not settle. A ketiv/qere note (single-witness apparatus) sits at oshb:Isa.42.20, inside this span; a second ketiv/qere note (single-witness apparatus) sits at oshb:Isa.42.24; both are disclosed here without adjudicating either specific reading. This span's own bytes name a party in a different role: יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל לְבֹזְזִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.42.24, tier: byte) names Jacob and Israel as the ones given up to plunder; that naming is disclosed neutrally here, held open against the servant designation of web:Isa.42.19 and not resolved in either direction. This unit's own opening seam is straddled by the blindness lexeme: the clause וְהוֹלַכְתִּ֣י עִוְרִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.42.16, tier: byte) reaches into this unit's own onset, its own עִוְרִ֗ים re-collating against וְהַעִוְרִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.42.18, tier: byte) at accent_stripped tier and continuing at עִוֵּר֙ (oshb:Isa.42.19, tier: byte) (sweep: 5 verses, the blind lexeme in chs 42-43: oshb:Isa.42.7, 42.16, 42.18, 42.19, 43.8). The close seam is a cross-part seam and carries two further devices: וַתִּבְעַר בּ֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.25, tier: byte) is answered by וְלֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר בָּֽךְ (oshb:Isa.43.2, tier: byte), the two sharing only the fire-verb stem, the attested tokens returning tier NONE; and the same name-pair recurs at בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte), likewise stem-level against oshb:Isa.42.24.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: web:Isa.42.14 opens this unit, “I have been silent a long time. I have been quiet and restrained myself. Now I will cry out like a travailing woman. I will both gasp and pant., pointed הֶחֱשֵׁ֨יתִי֙ מֵֽעוֹלָ֔ם אַחֲרִ֖ישׁ אֶתְאַפָּ֑ק כַּיּוֹלֵדָ֣ה אֶפְעֶ֔ה אֶשֹּׁ֥ם וְאֶשְׁאַ֖ף יָֽחַד (oshb:Isa.42.14, tier: byte), a fresh first-person divine self-declaration opening a new speech distinct from the third-person hymn-call closing the previous span. A parashah SAMEKH mark, single-witness attested, is set at oshb:Isa.42.13, at the point just ahead of this unit's opening. It continues through the mountains-and-blind imagery, closing at web:Isa.42.17 with a rebuke of those who trust in engraved images and tell molten images they are gods. Marking this unit's own end at oshb:Isa.42.17 is a SAMEKH-type parashah mark (single-witness), which strengthens the seam ahead of the imperative address to the deaf and blind at oshb:Isa.42.18.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding oshb:Isa.42.17's idol-trust rebuke into the following span as its opening verse was proposed but not adopted, because the parashah SAMEKH mark closes at oshb:Isa.42.17 rather than before it, and the idol-trusters named there are third-person objects of the divine action described through oshb:Isa.42.14-Isa.42.16, not the deaf-and-blind addressees the imperative of oshb:Isa.42.18 opens with.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: divine self-declaration of intervention, closing in a rebuke of idol-trust
prev_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
prev_row.device_notes: The blind-guiding promise of web:Isa.42.16 anticipates the blind-servant address of web:Isa.42.18-Isa.42.19 in the following span; this row discloses the shared imagery as a cross-seam echo without merging the two spans, since the addressee and grammatical person both shift at web:Isa.42.18's imperative onset.

next_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens a fresh salvation oracle at the divine-frame onset וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier) -- one of four divine-owned koh-amar frames in this run of oracles, alongside כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, byte tier) earlier in the sequence (sweep: 4 verses, the koh-amar formula within chs 41-43 -- oshb:Isa.42.5, oshb:Isa.43.1, oshb:Isa.43.14, oshb:Isa.43.16, all four divine-owned) -- “But now Yahweh who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel, says:” “Don't be afraid, for I have redeemed you.” (web:Isa.43.1), pairing the creation verbs on the pointed page as בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier) -- Jacob and Israel named as the addressee here, not read as the servant of a trial speech. The fear-not formula repeats at “Don't be afraid, for I am with you.” (web:Isa.43.5) inside the same address, and the unit closes on the matching triad “everyone who is called by my name, and whom I have created for my glory, whom I have formed, yes, whom I have made.” (web:Isa.43.7), spliced at בְּרָאתִ֑יו יְצַרְתִּ֖יו אַף עֲשִׂיתִֽיו (oshb:Isa.43.7, byte tier): the created/formed/made sequence answers the opening pair and closes the unit ahead of the blind-people summons that opens web:Isa.43.8, the gathered-nations address itself not opening until web:Isa.43.9.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading extends the unit through the witness summons of Isa.43.8-Isa.43.9, treating both as one first-person divine address spanning the shift from the addressed nation to the gathered nations; the rival is refused because the address changes at web:Isa.43.9, כָּֽל הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו (oshb:Isa.43.9, byte tier), while web:Isa.43.8 opens a distinct summons of the blind people, הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר (oshb:Isa.43.8, byte tier) -- the same pointed word recurring at byte tier one part earlier, וְעִוֵּ֖ר כְּעֶ֥בֶד יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.42.19, byte tier), naming the LORD's own servant's blindness -- reaching back rather than forward into the nations' gathering.
next_row.literature_type_guess: salvation oracle assuring Jacob/Israel with a creation-verb inclusio
next_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
next_row.device_notes: The creator/form/make triad recurring later across the surrounding oracle sequence is read as a recurring vocabulary thread rather than a formal bracket-refrain reaching across this row's end seam; the row's own inclusio is bounded by the two fear-not addresses to Jacob and Israel by name. A fire-catchword pair straddles the row's own opening seam at the part boundary: וַתִּבְעַר בּ֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.25) against וְלֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר בָּֽךְ (oshb:Isa.43.2), sharing only the burn/kindle root, with the attested tokens matching at none of the byte, nfd, accent-stripped, or skeleton tiers (tier NONE), alongside the Jacob/Israel name pair recurring from יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל (oshb:Isa.42.24, the quoted run standing clear of that verse's ketiv/qere token pair, single-witness apparatus) to בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1) at stem level -- devices that argue continuity across the seam without disturbing the cut. The unit also carries an in-span title site, קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.43.3, byte tier), whose core re-collates at byte tier against the title closing the units at oshb:Isa.41.16 and oshb:Isa.41.20; here it is distinguished by position, standing inside an appositional divine self-identification with a further clause following, rather than in the verse's own closing clause as at those two sites.

queue_items.grounds: device_notes: the pair is said to share 'only the burn/kindle root, with the attested tokens matching at none of the byte, nfd, accent-stripped, or skeleton tiers (tier NONE)'. The claim is stated symmetrically and names skeleton explicitly among the tiers that fail, so it is false as written. It is also the disclosure on which the row rests its judgement that the cross-seam devices 'argue continuity across the seam without disturbing the cut', so the corrected tier changes the disclosed weight of a device on the row's own seam. The cut itself is unaffected: the onset וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte) is a tier-1 divine-speech frame.
queue_items.proposed_change: Restate as skeleton tier in the oshb:Isa.43.2 to oshb:Isa.42.25 direction and none in the reverse, keeping the continuity-without-disturbance judgement, which survives at skeleton tier.

queue_items.claim: The shared 43:7|43:8 seam is argued incompatibly by this row and its book-order neighbor: this row's refusal ground places 43:8's affinity backward, away from the very unit the neighbor row opens at 43:8.
queue_items.grounds: This row refuses its rival because עִוֵּ֖ר stands at oshb:Isa.43.8 as 'a distinct summons of the blind people' whose byte-tier tie runs to oshb:Isa.42.19 -- 'reaching back rather than forward into the nations' gathering'. The neighbor row makes oshb:Isa.43.8 the onset verse of the gathering-trial unit and grounds that onset on a participant shift it discloses it cannot fix at form level. Both rows place the seam at the same point, so no span is in dispute; the stated affinity of the opening verse is. The byte tie itself verifies: עִוֵּ֖ר (oshb:Isa.43.8, tier: byte) returns BYTE tier against oshb:Isa.42.19.
queue_items.proposed_change: Reconcile the two rows' stated grounds for the 43:7|43:8 seam so the blind-word tie is described the same way on both sides -- a backward lexical echo carried by a verse that nonetheless opens the following unit -- without moving the seam.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens a fresh salvation oracle at the divine-frame onset וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier) -- one of four divine-owned koh-amar frames in this run of oracles, alongside כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, byte tier) earlier in the sequence (sweep: 4 verses, the koh-amar formula within chs 41-43 -- oshb:Isa.42.5, oshb:Isa.43.1, oshb:Isa.43.14, oshb:Isa.43.16, all four divine-owned) -- “But now Yahweh who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel, says:” “Don't be afraid, for I have redeemed you.” (web:Isa.43.1), pairing the creation verbs on the pointed page as בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier) -- Jacob and Israel named as the addressee here, not read as the servant of a trial speech. The fear-not formula repeats at “Don't be afraid, for I am with you.” (web:Isa.43.5) inside the same address, and the unit closes on the matching triad “everyone who is called by my name, and whom I have created for my glory, whom I have formed, yes, whom I have made.” (web:Isa.43.7), spliced at בְּרָאתִ֑יו יְצַרְתִּ֖יו אַף עֲשִׂיתִֽיו (oshb:Isa.43.7, byte tier): the created/formed/made sequence answers the opening pair and closes the unit ahead of the blind-people summons that opens web:Isa.43.8, the gathered-nations address itself not opening until web:Isa.43.9.
